title: Endobronchial Valves for Persistent Air Leak and Bronchopleural Fistula in Children: A Systematic Review of Indications, Procedural Approaches, and Outcomes.
authors: Mahindrakar N, Bhandari P, Yedatore R, Vorakunthada Y, Lilitwat W
abstract: BACKGROUND: Persistent air leak (PAL) and bronchopleural fistula (BPF) are uncommon but important complications in children, particularly with necrotizing pneumonia, postoperative injury, malignancy, or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). When conservative therapy fails or surgery is high-risk, endobronchial or intrabronchial valve placement has emerged as a minimally invasive bronchoscopic option. This systematic review summarizes the published pediatric experience, focusing on indications, procedural approach, and outcomes. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to June 2026, with Google Scholar and reference lists screened; no language limits applied. Eligible studies reported pediatric or late-adolescent patients who underwent bronchoscopic valve placement for PAL, BPF, or pneumothorax with ongoing air leak. Case reports, case series, and observational studies with extractable pediatric data were included. Two reviewers independently screened, assessed eligibility, and abstracted data; findings were synthesized narratively. RESULTS: Thirteen reports were included. Valve placement achieved rapid or eventual air-leak improvement in selected children, including those with necrotizing pneumonia, postoperative air leak, chronic ventilator dependence, malignancy, and ECMO support. Reported complications included valve migration or loosening, granulation tissue, minor hemoptysis, atelectasis, contralateral pneumothorax, and recurrent air leak, although many children underwent valve removal without complication. CONCLUSION: Endobronchial or intrabronchial valve placement may be a useful rescue or bridge therapy for carefully selected children with refractory PAL or BPF. Evidence remains low certainty owing to small samples, retrospective design, inconsistent outcome definitions, and possible publication bias. Prospective multicenter registries with standardized reporting are needed to define optimal selection, timing, and safety.

title: MHC-II deficiency in a large Algerian cohort: Clinical, immunological, and genetic characterization.
authors: Lamara Mahammed L, Belaid B, Chan KW, Mohand-Oussaid A, Drali O, Dehimi A, Leung D, Berkani LM
abstract: MHC class II (MHC-II) deficiency is a rare inborn error of immunity caused by defects in transcriptional regulators of MHC-II expression. In this study, we characterized the clinical, immunological, and molecular features of 107 patients from 98 unrelated Algerian families. Median ages at symptom onset and diagnosis were 5 and 14 mo, respectively, with pneumonia (82%) and chronic diarrhea (73%) predominating. CD4+ T cell lymphopenia occurred in 87.6% and naïve CD4+ T cell depletion in 86.0%. Among 99 genetically characterized patients, variants were identified exclusively in RFXANK (77.8%) and RFXAP (22.2%), including two predominant mutations (RFXANK c.338-25_338del and RFXAP c.368del) and four novel variants. Exploratory comparisons suggested a more severe phenotype in patients carrying RFXAP c.368del than in those carrying RFXANK c.338-25_338del. Five of seven transplanted patients survived versus 33.3% of non-transplanted patients. As the largest MHC-II deficiency cohort reported to date, this study substantially expands current knowledge of the disease and supports targeted genetic diagnosis in North African populations.

title: The Lipid Paradox in Chronic Liver Disease: Integrative Evidence From Intrahepatic Transcriptomics and Population-based Cohorts.
authors: Su S, Chen Z, Ye Y, Yin W, Li F, Liu A
journal: Journal of clinical and experimental hepatology
abstract: BACKGROUND/AIMS: Chronic liver disease (CLD) is associated with major metabolic disturbances. Although an elevated atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) reflects cardiometabolic risk, progressive liver dysfunction may instead be accompanied by lipid depletion, suggesting a "lipid paradox." We aimed to investigate its intrahepatic transcriptomic basis, systemic manifestations, and clinical implications using an integrative molecular-to-population approach. METHODS: Intrahepatic transcriptomic data from the Gene Expression Omnibus were analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes associated with chronic hepatitis B progression, and hub genes were screened by machine learning. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2015-2018 data were used to examine the association between the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) and AIP using survey-weighted models and mediation analyses. Data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) were used to model 4-yr AIP trajectories and explore associations with cardiometabolic outcomes and all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Transcriptomics identified nine immune-fibrotic hub genes; functional enrichment showed immune activation and matrix remodeling with suppressed lipid metabolism. In NHANES, higher fibrosis risk was independently associated with lower AIP, with mediation more consistent with metabolic depletion than inflammation and independent of the age term in FIB-4. In CHARLS, individuals with liver disease showed an attenuated AIP trajectory; within this subgroup, lower AIP was associated with a higher prevalence of cardiovascular disease and metabolic syndrome, with an exploratory adverse survival signal. CONCLUSION: Across transcriptomic, cross-sectional, and longitudinal analyses, reduced AIP in CLD may reflect metabolic and nutritional vulnerability rather than cardiometabolic protection, warranting further evaluation as an indicator for risk stratification.

title: Comorbid asthma - occurrence and associations with patient-related outcomes in COPD: a cohort study.
authors: Athlin Å, Lisspers K, Hasselgren M, Ställberg B, Sandelowsky H, Giezeman M, Janson C, Kisiel MA
journal: Scandinavian journal of primary health care
abstract: PURPOSE: Clinical features of COPD and asthma overlap, complicating differential diagnosis. This study investigated the prevalence of comorbid asthma in COPD patients and its association with patient-related outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients with a doctor's diagnosis of COPD were randomly selected in two cohorts 2005 (n = 1060) and 2014 (n = 1671), from primary and secondary care in Sweden. Data were collected from medical records and patient questionnaires at baseline and at follow-up (2012 and 2022, respectively). Questionnaires included data on exacerbations. Symptoms were assessed using the clinical COPD questionnaire (CCQ). Comorbid asthma was identified through medical records. Ten-year mortality data were obtained from national registers. Logistic and linear regression assessed associations with patient-reported outcomes; Cox regression was applied for mortality analyses. RESULTS: Comorbid asthma was found in 22% of the 2005 cohort and 9% of the 2014 cohort (p < .001). In both cohorts, it was associated with an increased risk of exacerbations: OR (95% CI) 1.58 (1.07-2.32), p = .02, and 2.20 (1.38-3.52), p < .001, respectively. No associations were found between comorbid asthma and worsening of health status (CCQ). Mortality risk did not differ in the 2005 cohort, HR (95% CI) 0.92 (0.71-1.18), but was lower in the 2014 cohort, HR (95% CI) 0.67 (0.49-0.93), p = .02. CONCLUSION: Comorbid asthma in COPD has changed from 22 to 9%, potentially due to improved diagnostics. Comorbid asthma remains clinically relevant due to its association with an increased exacerbation risk.

title: Acute Kidney Disease and Clinical Outcomes in Stable Outpatients With Decompensated Cirrhosis: A Prospective Cohort Study.
authors: Lekakis V, Wong F, Papatheodoridis G, Vlachogiannakos J, Cholongitas E
journal: Journal of clinical and experimental hepatology
abstract: BACKGROUND/AIMS: Acute kidney disease (AKD), as recently redefined by the Acute Disease Quality Initiative-International Club of Ascites (ADQI-ICA) consensus, captures persistent or subacute kidney dysfunction often following acute kidney injury (AKI). Its prognostic relevance in stable outpatients with decompensated cirrhosis remains insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of AKD and its phenotypes (AKI-AKD and non-AKI AKD [NAKI-AKD]) with cirrhosis-related complications and mortality in outpatients with stable decompensated cirrhosis. METHODS: In this prospective real-world study, 131 patients were followed for up to 60 mo. AKD was defined according to ADQI-ICA criteria and modeled as a time-dependent exposure. Complications were analyzed using Poisson incidence rate and cause-specific Cox models. Mortality was assessed using Aalen-Johansen estimates and time-dependent cause-specific Cox regression, with liver transplantation considered a competing event and parsimonious adjustment for baseline liver disease severity. RESULTS: AKD developed in 51 patients (38.9%). The overall complication-event rate was higher following AKD onset than during AKD-free follow-up (183.3 vs 36.6 per 100 person-years; adjusted incidence rate ratio: 4.91, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 3.01-8.03; P < 0.001). In the MELD 3.0-adjusted model, the mortality hazard was highest during the AKD period (0-90 d after onset [adjusted cause-specific hazard ratio (aCsHR): 27.07, 95% CI: 11.83-61.90; P < 0.001]) and remained elevated during the late follow-up after AKD (aCsHR: 8.77, 95% CI: 4.00-19.23; P < 0.001). Among patients with AKD, AKI-AKD was associated with higher mortality than NAKI-AKD (aCsHR: 3.07, 95% CI: 1.46-6.47; P = 0.003). CONCLUSION: AKD is common among stable outpatients with decompensated cirrhosis and was associated with a graded risk of complications and death. Phenotypic stratification identifies AKI-AKD as the highest-risk subgroup, although these findings require confirmation in larger prospective studies.

title: Evaluating a Modified American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status-Based Sedation Management System for Pancreatobiliary Endoscopy: A Prospective Feasibility Study.
authors: Hanaoka T, Okuwaki K, Watanabe M, Matsuda H, Adachi K, Tamaki A, Ogawa D, Sakai M
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To prospectively evaluate the feasibility of implementing a modified American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status (ASA-PS)-based sedation management system for endoscopist-managed sedation in pancreatobiliary endoscopy. METHODS: This single-center, single-arm prospective feasibility study involved 2000 patients (2024-2025). Sedation risk was stratified using a modified ASA-PS classification system combined with predefined high-risk clinical factors (severe obesity, obstructive sleep apnea requiring continuous positive airway pressure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease requiring home oxygen therapy, reduced functional capacity, and difficult sedation history). Patients meeting high-risk criteria underwent pre-procedural anesthesiologist assessment to determine sedation providers. The primary outcome was sedation-related adverse event (SRAE) incidence during endoscopist-managed sedation. The secondary outcomes were the sedation success rate and SRAE-associated risk factors. RESULTS: Among 2000 patients, 231 (11.6%) were classified as having high risk for sedation. Post-assessment, anesthesiologists and endoscopists managed sedation for 86 (4.3%) and 1914 (95.7%) patients, respectively. In the endoscopist-managed group, SRAEs occurred in 63 patients (3.3%), corresponding to a success rate of 96.7%. No patient required tracheal intubation or conversion to general anesthesia. In multivariable analysis, endoscopic ultrasonography-guided sampling was independently associated with reduced SRAEs (odds ratio 0.407, 95% confidence interval 0.184-0.899; p = 0.026); no independent predictors of increased SRAEs were identified. CONCLUSIONS: The modified ASA-PS-based sedation management system may be a feasible approach in settings with limited anesthesiology resources, warranting further validation. title: Reprogramming the therapeutic fate of living biotherapeutic products for intestinal diseases via biomaterials.
authors: Cheng X, Yang Y, Ding H, Huang R, Cao S, Shi R, Qi G, Wang S
abstract: Live biotherapeutic products (LBP) hold great promise for the treatment of intestinal diseases such as inflammatory bowel disease and colorectal cancer, owing to their unique abilities to modulate the gut microbiota, regulate host immunity, and influence drug metabolism. However, the use of natural strains remains constrained by several challenges, including poor survival, limited colonization efficiency, immune clearance and non-specific targeting. Rational engineering of bacteria can overcome these limitations, while biomaterials, owing to their safety and versatile functionalities, provide powerful tools for bacterial modification. Recent studies have focused on developing biomaterial-modified bacteria (BMB) using lipid-based coatings, hydrogels, organic-inorganic hybrid materials, antibody or functional protein and cell membrane. This review systematically summarizes strategies for modifying bacterial surfaces with these biomaterials, elucidates the underlying mechanisms by which they enhance bacterial performance, and highlights recent advances in this field, offering insights that may inspire the design of the next generation of BMB based on high-throughput platforms, synthetic biology, and artificial intelligence (AI).

title: A topologically engineered hydrogel platform targeting IL11 promotes renal repair after partial nephrectomy.
authors: Yu Z, Dong X, Li F, Zhang Y, Dai S, Cao N, Jia X, Zhao J
abstract: Partial nephrectomy (PN) is the gold standard for treating renal tumors and trauma; however, massive nephron loss and persistent fibrosis readily lead to chronic kidney disease (CKD). Current therapeutic options remain non-curative and costly, as nearly half of PN patients inevitably progress to end-stage renal failure. Here, we present an innovative regenerative platform for PN-induced CKD, integrating structural biomimicry with targeted molecular inhibition. Harnessing light-based bioprinting of gelatin and hyaluronic acid methacrylates coupled with removable alginate microfiber, we constructed a hierarchical channel scaffold (HCS) that features precisely patterned macrochannels and template-derived microchannels, which closely mimics native kidney architecture, provides structural support, and remarkably enhances cell migration (∼5.45-fold) and rapid neovascularization (∼7.66-fold) over unidirectional channel structures. Moreover, interleukin 11 (IL11) was identified as a novel therapeutic target in kidney fibrosis after PN. Thus, extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from mesenchymal stem cells loaded with IL11 small interfering RNA (siIL11) were homogeneously encapsulated into HCS, achieving over 4-fold higher renal retention than systemic delivery in PN-induced CKD mice. Furthermore, sustained local release of EV-siIL11 and hierarchically channeled HCS guided synergistic regenerative effects that remarkably inhibited fibrosis, cell cycle arrest, and immune responses, thereby potently preventing kidney atrophy and restoring renal structure with newly aligned nephrons and vasculature, ultimately recovering kidney function. Further analysis revealed that IL11 silencing reversed epithelial‒mesenchymal transition by suppressing the STAT3-ERK-GSK3β-SNAI1 axis. This topological multifunctional hydrogel platform offers a localized, sustained, and clinically translatable strategy for postsurgical kidney regeneration.

title: Spatial mechanopriming of multicellular interfaces drives cytoskeletal-to-nuclear remodeling to boost therapeutic efficacy of stem cells.
authors: Bayaraa O, Lee NH, Kim SH, Lee H, Li CJ, Fu X, Hyun J, Choi G
abstract: Engineering multicellular constructs through biophysical cues, independent of soluble biochemical factors, is a promising strategy to boost the therapeutic potential of stem cells for regenerative medicine. However, the mechanisms by which spatially organized cell-cell and cell-matrix interfaces govern multicellular signaling and subsequent behavioral outcomes remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate these mechanistic events by introducing 2D nanoplates (∼350 nm) compartmentalized within the intercellular space of mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) spheroids to form de novo cell-matrix spatial interfaces. These interfaces redistribute internal stress across the spheroid, amplifying integrin-cytoskeleton-nucleus force transmission and restoring YAP-dependent mechanotransduction to achieve spatial mechanopriming. Cells within these mechanoprimed spheroids exhibit profound nuclear deformation, epigenetic remodeling, and spatially patterned metabolic activation. Finite element modeling and spatial transcriptomic analyses further reveal a spheroid-wide reorganization of cytoskeletal and transcriptional networks. Mechanistically, elevated cytoskeletal tension across the reorganized interfaces is associated with a putative, tension-associated pseudo-hypoxic signature involving HIF-1α-related signaling, establishing a mechanometabolic niche that robustly enhances angiogenic secretion. Consequently, mechanoprimed spheroids demonstrate superior engraftment, accelerated vascular regeneration, and improved perfusion recovery in a murine ischemia model. Collectively, this work establishes spatial mechanopriming as an effective strategy to remodel cytoskeletal-to-nuclear mechanics and enhance the therapeutic potential of 3D multicellular systems.

title: Tissue engineering polymeric formulations enable lymphangiogenesis for myocardial repair.
authors: Liu Z, Li R, Huang W, Zhang J, Qu Y, Dong W, Liu Y, Li Q
abstract: PURPOSE: Emerging evidence emphasizes the pivotal contribution of cardiac lymphatic activation following ischemic heart injury, with induced lymphangiogenesis driving edema resolution and inflammatory cell clearance. The aim of this study was to identify a bioactive small molecule with pro-lymphangiogenic activity and to develop a tissue engineering polymeric formulation for sustained local delivery in myocardial repair. METHODS: Through a high-throughput screen, we identified the bioactive molecule β-(3,4-dihydroxyphenyl) lactic acid (3,4-DHPLA) as a potent stimulator of lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs). To leverage this finding, we engineered a tissue engineering polymeric formulation (TEPF) to promote lymphangiogenesis during myocardial repair. The TEPF was fabricated via an integrated strategy combining 3D printing and near-field electrospinning to incorporate 3,4-DHPLA into a biodegradable polyurethane scaffold. The resulting structure mimics the microstructure of the cardiac extracellular matrix while supporting the microenvironment-responsive release of 3,4-DHPLA. RESULTS: We evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of TEPF in rat and porcine ischemia/reperfusion injury models, which markedly improved cardiac function and significantly attenuated adverse ventricular remodeling. Single-cell RNA sequencing and in vitro data further revealed the dual mechanisms of TEPF, not only promoting lymphangiogenesis but also orchestrating a pro-regenerative niche via expansion of Tregs, M2 macrophages, and pro-regenerative fibroblasts (COL12A1+, COL11A1+, NRG1+). CONCLUSIONS: Thus, the tissue engineering polymeric formulations may enable sustained drug release during myocardial tissue repair, thereby alleviating the pain of injection administration for patients with cardiovascular diseases and potentially facilitating patient-friendly use of other functional molecules-based therapeutic tissue engineering formulations through durable delivery.

title: Targeting the lactate/P300/H3K18la epigenetic pathway with a mechanoadaptive biomimetic hydrogel to suppress traumatic tendon heterotopic ossification.
authors: Feng H, Ang K, Deng Z, Cui C, Chen J, Huang N, Feng Y, Zhang J
abstract: Traumatic heterotopic ossification (HO) is a debilitating complication of tendon injury, yet its pathogenic mechanisms remain elusive and effective preventive strategies are lacking. Here, we identify a glycometabolic-epigenetic axis that drives HO progression. Single-cell profiling and functional analyses reveal that hypoxic chondrocytes undergo glycolytic reprogramming, leading to lactate accumulation and transfer into tendon-derived mesenchymal stem cells (TD-MSCs) through MCT1. This metabolic coupling promotes P300-dependent histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la), activating osteogenic programs characterized by Col6a1, Zhx3, Lox and Vdr expression and thereby facilitating pathological endochondral ossification. Guided by this mechanism, we develop a tendon-adhesive hydrogel (GelHA-A485@Exos) that integrates mechanical repair with targeted epigenetic modulation. MSC-derived exosomes enable localized delivery of the P300 inhibitor A485, suppressing H3K18la and aberrant osteogenic activation, while the hydrogel scaffold enhances tendon regeneration. In vivo and in vitro studies demonstrate that GelHA-A485@Exos promotes tendon healing while preventing HO formation. Our findings establish metabolic-epigenetic communication as a central regulator of traumatic HO and provide a translational therapeutic strategy for its clinical prevention.

title: Beyond stroke: atrial fibrillation and the broader burden of thromboembolic events in the population-based EpiHealth study.
authors: Höiby P, Zarrouk M, Lind L, Basna R, Overton MC, Elmståhl S
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the distribution and risk of thromboembolic events (TEs) among adults with and without atrial fibrillation (AF), and to assess oral anticoagulant (OAC) use over time. DESIGN: This population-based longitudinal cohort study included EpiHealth participants recruited between April 2011 and December 2016 and followed through linkage to Swedish health data registers from baseline until the first TE, death, or December 31, 2016. RESULTS: At baseline, 873 of 22,616 participants (3.9%) had AF and 297 developed incident AF during follow-up. 484 participants experienced at least one TE during 70,587 person-years. Participants with AF had higher TE incidence (68 events, 5.9%; p < 0.001), predominantly arterial (73.5%), with 94% of arterial events involving the cerebral circulation. Approximately one quarter of TEs among participants with AF occurred outside the cerebral circulation and comprised both venous and non-cerebral arterial events. Although participants with incident AF represented less than one quarter of participants with AF, they accounted for 40% of TEs in the AF group. OAC use increased from 39.0% to 50.4%, with a shift from predominantly warfarin to direct oral anticoagulants. In time-dependent Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, and prior arterial thromboembolism, untreated AF was associated with increased thromboembolic risk compared with no AF (HR 2.53), whereas OAC use was associated with lower risk. CONCLUSIONS: AF was associated with substantially increased thromboembolic risk, predominantly arterial in nature. One in five TEs among participants with AF coincided with newly diagnosed AF, suggesting potential opportunities for earlier AF detection and timely initiation of anticoagulant treatment.

title: Circulatory arrest versus aortic cross-clamping in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm repair.
authors: Braatz E, Stenman M, Al-Mousli J, Dalén M, Olsson C
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aortic cross‑clamping and mild hypothermic circulatory arrest (MHCA) are commonly used strategies in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm surgery. This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. The primary outcome was a composite of 30‑day mortality, stroke, or acute kidney injury, with secondary outcomes including long‑term survival and postoperative complications. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This single‑center observational cohort included patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Distal ascending aortic diameters were assessed on preoperative computed tomography, and clinical data were obtained from SWEDEHEART. Patients were assigned to aortic cross‑clamp (n = 261) or MHCA (n = 138). Propensity score matching was performed in a 1:1 ratio to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: The composite primary outcome occurred in 15 patients (3.8%) and was more common with MHCA than with cross‑clamp (6.5% vs 2.3%, p = 0.035). Two patients (0.5%), both in the MHCA group, died within 30 days. After matching, the odds ratio for the composite endpoint was 2.4 (95% CI, 0.66-11.5), indicating no significant difference. Long‑term survival was similar between groups (log‑rank p = 0.33). CONCLUSIONS: Both strategies were associated with low perioperative risk and comparable long‑term survival. These results support flexible operative planning, allowing the distal anastomotic technique to be chosen based on individual anatomy and surgical preference.
publication_types: Journal Article, Comparative Study, Observational Study

title: Biomimetic sequential targeted nanoplatform for synergistic thrombolysis in ischemic stroke.
authors: Wang J, Wang X, Liu S, Zheng Y, Wang C, Cheng J, Wang X
abstract: Conventional thrombolytic drugs for vascular blockage such as tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) are challenged by the low bioavailability, off-target side effects and limited penetration in thrombi, leading to delayed recanalization. Herein, we developed a sequential targeted nanoplatform for efficient thrombolysis based on the thrombolysis-neuroprotection integrated strategy. The mesoporous silica layer-modified upconversion nanoparticle (UCNP) was loaded with the nitric oxide (NO) donors (BNN6), further coating platelet membranes (PMs) on the surface of UCNP. tPA was conjugated onto PMs using the MMP9-responsive peptide as a linker to form a multifunctional drug carrier of UCNP/BNN6@PM-tPA. The proposed drug carrier maintained stability in the blood circulation to reduce bleeding risk (protection), facilitating it colonizing at the thrombus clots. MMP-9 triggered the release of tPA to realize rapid thrombolysis (attack), whereas continuous NO release from NIR-irradiated BNN6 acted to prevent vascular re-embolization (defense). In vitro and in vivo evaluation revealed that UCNP/BNN6@PM-tPA enables thrombus-homing accumulation, fluorescence imaging-guided thrombolysis, and NO mediated prevention of thrombosis recurrence, displaying favorable therapeutic outcomes with low bleeding risk. This study offers a facile, safe, and effective way towards the clinical treatment of thrombosis and ischemic stroke.

title: Deformable yolk-shell nanoparticles for shear-driven tribocatalytic thrombolysis and cascade nanozyme-enabled recurrence prevention.
authors: Zheng H, Wang P, Huang P, Gao T, Wu Q, Wang J, Li X
abstract: Thrombotic diseases continue to pose a significant clinical challenge with high mortality and recurrence rates following thrombolysis. Herein, we propose endogenous shear stress-activated tribocatalytic thrombolysis via a dynamic S-scheme heterojunction and thrombosis recurrence-prevention via cascade nanozyme catalysis. Specifically, deformable yolk-shell nanoparticles (NPs) composed of bismuth ferrite-coated flexible mesoporous organosilica (fBF) yolks and manganese-doped cerium oxide (CeMn) shells, with fucoidan subsequently grafted onto the surface, are referred to as fBF@CeMn-Fu. Local shear stress induces high-frequency friction and collision between the fBF yolks and the CeMn shells, and tribocatalytic activity is promoted through friction contact area expansion via the deformability of mesoporous organosilica, S-scheme heterojunction between fBF and CeMn, and Mn-O-Ce electron channel and oxygen vacancies in CeMn. These deformability/component engineering and tribovoltaic/piezoelectric effect collectively boost electron-hole separation, overall redox capacity and generation of reactive oxygen species for effective thrombus dissolution. Upon completion of thrombolysis, Mn doping acts as a bidirectional electron pump, accelerating electron transfer and augmenting the superoxide dismutase (SOD) and catalase (CAT) activity of CeMn nanozyme. This SOD-CAT cascade catalysis effectively mitigates oxidative stress and inflammatory microenvironment associated with thrombosis, laying a foundation to prevent thrombosis recurrence. In a carotid artery thrombosis model, combination of tribocatalysis and fucoidan grafting achieve nearly complete thrombus dissolution. Subsequently, nanozyme cascade catalysis restores endothelial function, upregulates nitric oxide synthase expression, promotes endothelial healing, thereby suppressing platelet activation and thrombosis recurrence. The deformable yolks-enhanced tribocatalysis and nanozyme cascade offer an effective strategy for thrombosis management with precise dissolution and recurrence prevention.

title: Comprehensive analysis of peptide pharmaceutical: Development of three orthogonal chromatographic methods and characterization of bivalirudin degradation products by high-resolution mass spectrometry.
authors: Vukoja A, Pavić E, Galović S, Galić N
journal: Journal of pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis
abstract: Bivalirudin is a synthetic oligopeptide used as an anticoagulant for the treatment of acute coronary syndromes and for the prevention of thrombosis in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention. As peptides are complex molecules that may exhibit inherently complex impurity profiles, three orthogonal ultra-performance liquid chromatographic methods were developed in this work, in accordance with Analytical Quality-by-Design principles, to ensure the safety and efficacy of the bivalirudin drug product. Starting from a structure-driven theoretical assessment of bivalirudin, which anticipates the formation of peptide fragments, deamidation and oxidation products, as well as covalent oligomers under stress conditions, method development was directed into three orthogonal chromatographic modes-size-exclusion (SEC), reversed-phase (RP) and hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography (HILIC) - enabling a comprehensive evaluation of its degradation pathways. For the first time, bivalirudin oligomers (dimers and trimers) were detected and characterized using size-exclusion chromatography. The combination of HILIC and RP chromatography methods ensured separation of 10 non-oligomeric bivalirudin impurities. The developed methods employed MS-compatible mobile phases to facilitate structural elucidation of bivalirudin degradation products by high-resolution mass spectrometry. Stress conditions included acid and base hydrolysis, oxidation with H₂O₂, thermal decomposition, and light exposure, as regulated by ICH guidelines. Extensive risk assessment was conducted using Ishikawa diagrams and heat maps. Method development was carried out using Design of Experiments methodology, supported by Fusion AE software. The developed ultra-performance liquid chromatography (UPLC) methods were validated, confirming their suitability for analyzing bivalirudin and its related impurities.

title: Guanidine-quaternary ammonium polymer-derived carbon dots differentially modulate bacterial respiration and osteoblast mitochondria to resolve infection and foster osteointegration.
authors: Bai X, Qin A, Wang Z, Kong G, Zhang M, Li H, Zhao R, Yu Y
abstract: Implant-associated infections (IAIs) represent one of the most challenging complications following orthopedic implantation. Current antibacterial strategies struggle to achieve complete pathogen eradication while maintaining sustained osteogenic activity at the implant-bone interface. Leveraging the spatial divergence in energy metabolism between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, we designed and synthesized guanidine-quaternary ammonium polymer-derived carbon dots (GQCDs) with confirmed structure. Under non-infected conditions, GQCDs enhance mitochondrial metabolism to promote bone regeneration. In infected microenvironments, GQCDs not only selectively target bacterial membranes and inhibit the respiratory chain to exert potent antibacterial effects, but also downregulate host inflammatory responses and restore mitochondrial function in osteoblasts, thereby creating a favorable microenvironment for bone repair. GQCDs can be stably integrated onto various clinical implant substrates via a coating process. GQCDs-coated implants possessed the dual antibacterial and osteogenic functionalities, which were validated using in vitro co-culture systems and in vivo implant infection models in rats and beagles, offering a promising strategy with encouraging translational prospects to address IAIs.

title: Open-label extension study of leniolisib in activated PI3Kδ syndrome: Long-term efficacy and safety.
authors: Rao VK, Šedivá A, Dalm VASH, Plebani A, Schuetz C, Shcherbina A, Trizzino A, Zharankova Y
abstract: Activated phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta syndrome (APDS) is an inborn error of immunity characterized by immune deficiency and dysregulation. Leniolisib is a selective phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta inhibitor approved to treat APDS in patients ≥12 years old. We report final results from a single-arm, open-label extension study in 37 patients with APDS (NCT02859727). Median leniolisib exposure was 4.3 years (range, 1.2-7.0 years). Adverse events (AE) were reported in 34 patients; 87% were grade 1. Serious AEs, reported in 10 patients, were deemed unrelated to leniolisib. Two patients discontinued treatment due to AEs: cardiac arrest and Hodgkin's lymphoma. There were significant reductions in annual infection (P = 0.0005) and respiratory infection (P = 0.0017) rates per year of treatment. Immunoglobulin replacement therapy (IRT) use significantly decreased per year of treatment (P = 0.0095). Clinically meaningful improvements in general health scores from the 36-Item Short Form Survey were observed. Overall, long-term use of leniolisib was generally well tolerated, and infections and IRT use reduced over time.

title: 45th International Symposium on Intensive Care & Emergency Medicine.
Publication Only
Gut microbiota and metabolic characteristics in PWHIV with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).
authors: Liu H, Xu T, Guo Y, Zhou X, Yan C, Zhu B, Xie Y
abstract: The global prevalence of Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) among persons with HIV (PWHIV) is estimated at 34%. This study examined the influence of gut microbial and metabolic alterations in PWHIV with MASLD. We conducted 16S rRNA sequencing on 60 fecal samples (24 from HIV group and 36 from HIV-MASLD group) to assess microbial composition, and employed LC/MS-based metabolomics on both fecal and plasma samples to identify variations in metabolites. An exploratory analysis was performed to compare plasma cytokines and oxidative stress markers between the two groups. Sequencing in the HIV-MASLD group showed lower Faecalibacterium and Anaerobutyricum, and higher Klebsiella, Escherichia, and Enterococcus. Metabolomic analysis revealed a reduction in anti-inflammatory metabolites (Dodecanedioic acid, 5-Phenylvaleric acid, Kynurenic acid) and antioxidant metabolites, coupled with an increase in the pro-inflammatory metabolite Gamma-Glutamyl-L-Putrescine in the HIV-MASLD group. And plasma analysis indicated a decline in 20-carboxy arachidonic acid. Additionally, Faecalibacterium and Anaerobutyricum correlated positively with anti-inflammatory metabolites, while Klebsiella, Enterobacter, and Citrobacter correlated negatively. Furthermore, Faecalibacterium and Anaerobutyricum also showed a moderate negative correlation with MDA levels. A random forest model using plasma metabolites showed the optimal discriminative ability for HIV-MASLD (AUC = 0.819 ± 0.0059). Differences in gut microbiota and metabolites in PWHIV may affect MASLD progression by influencing inflammation and oxidative stress. Modulating gut microbiota, such as adding Faecalibacterium and Anaerobutyricum, could be a treatment strategy for HIV-MASLD. Plasma metabolites have potential as noninvasive markers.

title: Inflammation-anchored injectable hydrogel integrating pathological nitric oxide scavenging and on-demand drug release for localized inflammatory bowel disease therapy.
authors: Eom S, Lee S, Boo Y, Kim J, Kim WJ
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), encompassing chronic relapsing gastrointestinal disorders, remains a profound clinical challenge because conventional therapeutics are often impeded by systemic off-target toxicities and suboptimal retention at inflamed mucosal sites. Herein, an inflammation-activated and retentive injectable hydrogel is presented, which leverages pathological nitric oxide (NO) overproduction as both a therapeutic target and an autonomous release trigger. An NO-responsive and NO-scavenging polymer (NRSP) incorporating an NO-cleavable o-phenylenediamine (o-PD) motif is formulated into cationic, dexamethasone-encapsulating micelles and electrostatically assembled with anionic hyaluronic acid (HA) to form a shear-thinning hydrogel that facilitates minimally invasive rectal administration and ensures prolonged, localized retention at the inflamed mucosal interface. Upon exposure to the NO-rich inflammatory microenvironment, structural disruption of NO-responsive and NO-scavenging micelles (NRSM) compromises the electrostatic integrity of the HA-micelle network, thereby reducing the storage modulus and accelerating cargo release. In vitro evaluations using lipopolysaccharide-stimulated macrophages demonstrate that NRSM hydrogels effectively reduce intracellular and extracellular NO levels and attenuate pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion. Furthermore, the HA matrix mediates disease-adaptive localization through CD44 receptor recognition and preferential electrostatic adhesion to positively charged inflammatory interfaces, resulting in enhanced colonic retention in DSS-induced colitis models ex vivo. Following rectal administration in DSS-induced mice, NRSM-based hydrogels significantly alleviate disease severity, reduce colonic NO and inflammatory cytokine levels, and rescue mucosal architecture and mucin-associated features. Notably, dexamethasone-loaded NRSM hydrogel exerted the most potent synergistic therapeutic benefit. Overall, this disease-responsive hydrogel platform establishes an effective localized intervention for IBD, merging intrinsic pathological NO scavenging with controlled drug delivery.

title: Hematopoietic cell transplantation using treosulfan-based conditioning for IL-10 receptor deficiency.
authors: Lakkaraja M, Schmitt EG, Sood AK, Chen K, Modi AJ, Verbsky JW, Torgerson T, Wahbeh G
abstract: IL-10 receptor deficiency is a life-threatening inborn error of immunity associated with early-onset inflammatory bowel disease. Hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) using treosulfan-based conditioning resulted in excellent survival with full donor engraftment. Importantly, anakinra effectively served as a bridge to HCT.

Abstracts

Current Status of Bowel Preparation for Colonoscopy in Japan: A Web-Based Survey of Endoscopists (PRESS Survey).
authors: Matsumoto T, Esaki M, Hirai F, Umeyama M, Suzuki T, Takatsuki T, Shimada Y, Oota A
abstract: OBJECTIVES: The increasing number of patients with colorectal cancer underscores the importance of colonoscopy. Adequate bowel preparation is essential to ensure the quality and safety of colonoscopic examinations; however, data on the current practices in Japan remain limited. This study aimed to clarify the current status of bowel preparation, use of bowel-cleansing agents, and associated challenges among physicians performing colonoscopies. METHODS: In March 2026, we conducted a nationwide web-based cross-sectional survey of physicians performing colonoscopies in Japan. The survey assessed bowel preparation practices, use of bowel-cleansing agents, constipation, and renal function before colonoscopy. Responses were obtained from 300 physicians who performed at least 10 colonoscopies per month. RESULTS: Low-volume polyethylene glycol (PEG) plus ascorbate preparations were the most commonly used bowel-cleansing agents, followed by high-volume PEG preparations and magnesium-based agents. Cleansing efficacy and safety were the most highly valued characteristics of bowel-cleansing agents. 64.7% of physicians reported that the perceived frequency of inadequate bowel preparation was >10% among their patients. Although 64.3% of the physicians reported always assessing constipation, only 32.7% reported always evaluating renal function before colonoscopy. Compared with hospital-based physicians, those working in clinics reported a significantly lower proportion of inadequate bowel preparation, but a significantly lower rate of renal function assessment. CONCLUSION: Although cleansing efficacy and safety are prioritized in bowel preparation for colonoscopy in Japan, physicians perceived inadequate bowel preparation to occur in a substantial proportion of patients. Thus, further optimization of bowel preparation strategies and more consistent assessment of renal function before colonoscopy are needed. TRIAL REGISTRATION: University Hospital Medical Information Network (UMIN000060808).

title: Post-Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography Bleeding After Endoscopic Stone Removal in Dialysis Patients: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
authors: Nishimura M, Miwa H, Kaneko T, Kazuki E, Ritsuko O, Yuichi S, Hiromi T, Yoshimasa S
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Post-endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (post-ERCP) bleeding occurs more frequently in dialysis patients than in non-dialysis patients. This study aimed to identify risk factors for post-ERCP bleeding following stone removal in patients undergoing dialysis. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study enrolled 102 consecutive dialysis patients who underwent endoscopic stone removal at seven institutions between January 2009 and March 2022. Baseline characteristics, procedural details, stone removal outcomes, adverse events (AEs), and risk factors for post-ERCP bleeding were analyzed. RESULTS: Of the 102 patients, 65 were men. Median patient age was 77 years (range, 51-91 years). Antithrombotic drugs were administered to 64 patients (63%). Endoscopic sphincterotomy, endoscopic papillary balloon dilation, and endoscopic papillary large balloon dilation were performed in 58 (57%), 20 (20%), and 11 (11%) patients, respectively. AEs occurred in 23 patients (23%), including bleeding in eight patients (8%), acute pancreatitis in nine patients (9%), cholangitis in seven patients (7%), and others in two patients (2%). Multivariate analysis identified intraoperative bleeding and continued aspirin use as independent risk factors for post-ERCP bleeding. Similar associations were observed in subgroup analyses restricted to patients with a naïve papilla. CONCLUSIONS: Intraoperative bleeding and continued aspirin use were associated with post-ERCP bleeding following stone removal in dialysis patients, highlighting the importance of careful periprocedural hemostatic management in this population. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

title: LN-PMUT ultrasonic transducer enables instantaneous blood pressure reduction via renal hilar implantation.
authors: Ma J, Xing Z, Zhao Y, Sun C, Chen K, Ji W, Hu T, Wang J
abstract: Blood pressure (BP) is a fundamental vital sign, yet no implantable device for BP modulation is currently available. Here, we present a miniaturized ultrasound probe based on lead-free lithium niobate (LN) piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducer (PMUT) technology. The device features a dual-electrode design offering enhanced emission sensitivity and acoustic output, while maintaining a compact size (3 × 3 mm2, 3 mg), wide bandwidth (∼32%), and 2.5 MHz resonant frequency. Unilateral placement and vibratory stimulation at the renal hilum induced an immediate reduction in BP. Daily stimulation over one week reproducibly lowered BP, although the effect was limited to the stimulation period. Probe activation reduced renal vascular resistance and increased renal perfusion without observable structural damage or renal dysfunction within the study period. Transcriptomic sequencing of renal hilar tissue revealed bilateral nervous system changes following stimulation. Further analysis suggested that the hypotensive effect is partially mediated by sensory nerve release of calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP). Additionally, transcriptomic analysis revealed alterations in endocrine-related pathways on the stimulated side, particularly aldosterone-related pathways. In conclusion, renal hilar implantation of an LN-PMUT ultrasound probe achieves immediate BP reduction and may involve neural and endocrine pathway alterations associated with BP regulation, offering a potential strategy for the development of implantable BP regulators.

title: Hydrogen-bond interfacial engineering of silk fibroin-strengthened magnetic colloidal hydrogel for embolization and magnetothermal therapy of hepatocellular carcinoma.
authors: Chen B, Liu X, Hu J, Song Y, Hou X, Yan X, Dong L, Zhou T
abstract: Injectable hydrogels adapt to vascular shapes and block blood flow effectively, enabling wide application in the transcatheter arterial embolization (TAE) of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, balancing facile injectability and high mechanical robustness is challenging, as optimizing one compromises the other. Colloidal hydrogels achieve injectability via bottom-up assembly but have limited mechanical properties due to insufficient interface design. Herein, we report a hydrogen-bond interfacial strengthening strategy into the electrostatically crosslinked colloidal network to develop an injectable and mechanically stable magnetic colloidal hydrogel, which is assembled from electronegative hydrogen bond-rich silk fibroin iron oxide nanoparticles (SF@Fe3O4 NPs) and electropositive Gelatin NPs. This SF@Fe3O4 magnetic colloidal hydrogel (SF-MCH) can be injected through a medical microcatheter with an injection force of ∼10 N, which is only 15% of the manual limit. The storage modulus of SF-MCH (∼900 Pa) was three times higher than those of the PAA@Fe3O4 and Na3Cit@Fe3O4 magnetic colloidal hydrogels, meeting the mechanical performance requirements for embolization (>800 Pa), owing to the colloid interfacial hydrogen-bond interactions demonstrated by variable-temperature fourier transform infrared spectroscopy. Compared to gelatin bulk hydrogel containing SF@Fe3O4 NPs (SF-MBH), SF-MCH showed superior self-healing efficiency (94%) and shape fidelity. Additionally, SF-MCH could withstand pressures up to 36 kPa, well above physiological vascular pressure of 16 kPa. Furthermore, SF-MCH mediated embolization combined with magnetic hyperthermia significantly inhibited rabbit ear tumors, while SF-MCH achieved sustained renal artery embolization in rabbits. This hydrogen-bond interfacial reinforcing strategy brings a feasible route for the design of colloidal hydrogels with robust mechanics and tailor-made functionality.

title: Heterojunction nanozyme achieve highly efficient antibacterial by cuproptosis-like death and ferroptosis-like death.
authors: Wang W, Zhu R, Gui H, Jin X, Wei X, Wang X
abstract: Metal-ion-mediated lethal pathways offers a highly potent strategy for antibacterial treatments. However, relying on single-pathway mechanisms often fails to overwhelm bacterial antioxidant defenses, reducing antibacterial efficacy. This study designed a heterojunction nanozyme (Cu2O/Fe2O3) that induces ferroptosis-like death and copper-mediated metabolic toxicity exhibiting cuproptosis-like features, achieving highly effective antibacterial treatment. Computational chemistry analysis indicates that the Cu2O/Fe2O3 heterointerface establishes a built-in electric field through spontaneous interfacial electron transfer, thereby enhancing its peroxidase (POD)-like activity. Within the acidic bacterial microenvironment, Cu2O/Fe2O3 catalyzes the generation of large amounts of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and releases metal ions, inducing and amplifying ferroptosis-like death, which disrupts the function of ETC enzymes by attacking iron-sulfur clusters. Concurrently, copper ions disrupt the redox balance by depleting bacillithiol (BSH), indirectly increasing bacterial susceptibility and promoting ferroptosis-like death. Furthermore, the accumulation of copper ions triggers severe metabolic impairments that biochemically resemble the cuproptosis cascade, which disrupts key enzymes of the TCA cycle and impairs the synthesis of electron donors (NADH and FADH2), thereby cutting off the supply of substrates to ETC at the upstream stage. Overall, this study demonstrates that triggering bimetallic ion-mediated metabolic disruptions induces an energy crisis in bacteria, providing a reference for multimodal antibacterial strategies.

title: Microbial succession and genome-resolved metabolic functions shape flavor evolution during sauce-flavor Baijiu fermentation.
authors: Niu J, Li W, Chen X, Zhu H, Sun W, Li X, Sun B
abstract: Sauce-flavor Baijiu (SFB) fermentation is characterized by a unique multi-round solid-state process, during which complex microbial succession drives flavor formation. However, the functional differentiation and metabolic mechanisms of microbial communities across successive fermentation rounds remain poorly understood. In this study, the physicochemical properties, microbial assembly, and metabolic profiles of fermented grains (FG) were investigated across seven production rounds (R1-R7). The results revealed that as fermentation rounds progressed, the FG environment evolved toward elevated acidity and reduced pH, driving a directional shift in the microbial community from an initially diverse assemblage to a structure dominated by acid-tolerant Acetilactobacillus, which established pronounced ecological dominance in later rounds. Metabolomic analysis further indicated that this dynamic adjustment of microbial structure drove the evolution of the flavor profile, specifically manifesting as differential accumulation of compounds such as esters, alcohols, and pyrazines across the various rounds. Co-occurrence network analysis demonstrated that positive microbial interactions significantly predominated within the fermentation system, and that community function exhibited a convergent trend as the rounds increased. Furthermore, 158 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) were recovered, and metabolic reconstruction elucidated the potential contributions of genera such as Pediococcus, Bacillus, and Oceanobacillus to key metabolic pathways, including glycolysis, phenylalanine metabolism, and pyrazine biosynthesis. This work provides important insights into microbial regulation and quality improvement in SFB fermentation.
